sets.title: Measuring a Melting Glacier
sets.titleEs: Medir un glaciar que se derrite

learn.rule: Start with a kernel sentence (who + what). Then expand it by answering when, where, and why.
learn.ruleEs: Empieza con una oración base (quién + qué). Luego amplíala respondiendo cuándo, dónde y por qué.
learn.model: Last summer, researchers measured the glacier in Alaska to learn how fast it is thinning.
learn.notice: The kernel is Researchers measured the glacier. Each added detail answers one question: when, where, or why.

items.prompt: Which question does the phrase every July answer in the glacier sentence?
items.text: Researchers measured the glacier's thickness every July using radar on the Mendenhall Glacier in Alaska.
items.why: Every July tells when the measuring happens. Time words and phrases answer the question when.
items.whyEs: Every July dice cuándo se hace la medición. Las palabras y frases de tiempo responden la pregunta cuándo.

items.prompt: Which part of the glacier sentence answers where?
items.text: Researchers measured the glacier's thickness every July using radar on the Mendenhall Glacier in Alaska.

options.text: on the Mendenhall Glacier in Alaska

items.why: Place details answer where. On the Mendenhall Glacier in Alaska names the location.
items.whyEs: Los detalles de lugar responden dónde. On the Mendenhall Glacier in Alaska nombra la ubicación.

items.prompt: Which part of the ice sentence answers why?
items.text: The ice thins rapidly in summer because warm air and sunlight melt the surface.

options.text: because warm air and sunlight melt the surface

items.why: Why details explain the reason or cause. Because warm air and sunlight melt the surface is the reason the ice thins.
items.whyEs: Los detalles de por qué explican la razón o la causa. Because warm air and sunlight melt the surface es la razón por la que el hielo se adelgaza.

items.prompt: Choose the detail that tells WHEN.
parts: The research team collected ice cores
from the summit of the glacier.
items.model: The research team collected ice cores last August from the summit of the glacier.
items.why: Last August is a time detail, so it answers when. With a steel drill tells how, and in the lab would tell where.
items.whyEs: Last August es un detalle de tiempo, así que responde cuándo. With a steel drill dice cómo, e in the lab diría dónde.

items.prompt: Check every expansion of The glacier is retreating that adds when or where.

options.text: The glacier is retreating faster each decade.
The glacier is retreating, which worries scientists.
The tall glacier is retreating up its valley.
The glacier is retreating, and it is large.

items.why: Each decade tells when and up its valley tells where. The other two add an opinion or a size, not a time or a place.
items.whyEs: Each decade dice cuándo y up its valley dice dónde. Las otras dos agregan una opinión o un tamaño, no un tiempo ni un lugar.

items.prompt: Which is the strongest expansion of the kernel The scientists published a report?

options.text: The scientists published a long report yesterday.
After a five-year study, glaciologists published a report in a scientific journal explaining why the Alaskan ice is thinning.

items.why: The strongest sentence answers several questions at once: when (after a five-year study), where (in a journal), and why (explaining the thinning).
items.whyEs: La oración más fuerte responde varias preguntas a la vez: cuándo (after a five-year study), dónde (in a scientific journal) y por qué (explaining the thinning).

write.prompt: Expand the kernel sentence. Tell when and where the scientists measured the ice, and add why if you can.
write.promptEs: Amplía la oración base. Di cuándo y dónde midieron el hielo los científicos, y agrega por qué si puedes.
write.model: Last summer, the scientists measured the ice on a glacier in Alaska to learn how quickly it was thinning.

familyTalk.en: Say a short sentence like 'We cooked.' Take turns adding when, where, and why until it is a full story.
familyTalk.es: Digan una oración corta como 'Cocinamos.' Túrnense para agregar cuándo, dónde y por qué hasta formar una historia completa.

teacherTip.en: Write the kernel on the board and color-code each added detail by question (when, where, why) as students build.
teacherTip.es: Escribe la oración base en el pizarrón y codifica con colores cada detalle agregado según la pregunta (cuándo, dónde, por qué).

sets.title: Roman Water Highways
sets.titleEs: Las autopistas de agua de Roma

learn.rule: Start with a kernel sentence (who + what). Then expand it by answering when, where, and why.
learn.ruleEs: Empieza con una oración base (quién + qué). Luego amplíala respondiendo cuándo, dónde y por qué.
learn.model: Over two thousand years ago, Romans built aqueducts across their empire so growing cities could have fresh water.
learn.notice: The kernel is Romans built aqueducts. Over two thousand years ago tells when, across their empire tells where, and so growing cities... tells why.

items.prompt: Which part of the aqueduct sentence answers where?
items.text: Roman engineers built aqueducts across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East to carry fresh water into growing cities.

options.text: to carry fresh water into growing cities
across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East

items.why: Across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East names the places, so it answers where.
items.whyEs: Across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East nombra los lugares, así que responde dónde.

items.prompt: Which part of the aqueduct sentence answers why?
items.text: Roman engineers built aqueducts across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East to carry fresh water into growing cities.

options.text: to carry fresh water into growing cities
across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East

items.why: To carry fresh water into growing cities gives the purpose, which answers why the engineers built them.
items.whyEs: To carry fresh water into growing cities da el propósito, que responde por qué los ingenieros las construyeron.

items.prompt: What question does the phrase during the empire's peak answer?
items.text: During the empire's peak, Rome received water through eleven aqueducts.
items.why: During the empire's peak tells the time period, so it answers when.
items.whyEs: During the empire's peak indica el período, así que responde cuándo.

items.prompt: Choose the detail that tells WHERE the water came from.
parts: to the fountains in the city.
items.model: The aqueduct carried water from mountain springs to the fountains in the city.
items.why: From mountain springs names a place, so it answers where. During the empire tells when, and with great pride does not answer any of the questions.
items.whyEs: From mountain springs nombra un lugar, así que responde dónde. During the empire dice cuándo, y with great pride no responde ninguna de las preguntas.

items.prompt: Check every expansion of The aqueduct still stands that adds when or where.

options.text: The aqueduct still stands in Segovia, Spain, after nearly two thousand years.
The aqueduct still stands, which is amazing.
The tall stone aqueduct still stands near the old city center.
The aqueduct still stands and is old.

items.why: In Segovia, Spain and near the old city center answer where, and after nearly two thousand years answers when. The others add only an opinion or a plain fact.
items.whyEs: In Segovia, Spain y near the old city center responden dónde, y after nearly two thousand years responde cuándo. Las otras solo agregan una opinión o un dato simple.

items.prompt: Which is the strongest expansion of the kernel Engineers built channels?

options.text: More than two thousand years ago, Roman engineers built long stone channels across valleys so cities could receive fresh water.

items.why: The strongest sentence says when, where, and why. The other two stay short and leave the reader with questions.
items.whyEs: La oración más fuerte dice cuándo, dónde y por qué. Las otras dos son cortas y dejan preguntas al lector.

write.prompt: Expand the kernel sentence. Tell when and where the Romans built aqueducts, and add why if you can.
write.promptEs: Amplía la oración base. Di cuándo y dónde construyeron acueductos los romanos, y agrega por qué si puedes.
write.model: Over two thousand years ago, Romans built aqueducts across their empire so growing cities could have fresh water.

familyTalk.en: Talk about a building or bridge in your city. Say when it was built, where it is, and why people use it.
familyTalk.es: Hablen de un edificio o puente de su ciudad. Digan cuándo se construyó, dónde está y por qué la gente lo usa.

teacherTip.en: Have students find the when, where, and why in the text on aqueducts before they expand their own kernel sentence.
teacherTip.es: Pide que busquen el cuándo, el dónde y el por qué en el texto sobre acueductos antes de ampliar su propia oración base.

learn.rule: Start with a kernel sentence (who + what). Then expand it by answering when, where, and why.
learn.ruleEs: Empieza con una oración base (quién + qué). Luego amplíala respondiendo cuándo, dónde y por qué.
learn.model: When the lights came on, Leila walked onto the stage in the town square and began to sing.
learn.notice: The kernel is Leila walked onto the stage. Added details tell when (the lights came on) and where (in the town square).

items.prompt: Which part of the festival sentence answers when?
items.text: On the last night of the festival, Leila waited nervously beside the stage while the crowd grew louder.

options.text: On the last night of the festival

items.why: On the last night of the festival tells when the scene takes place.
items.whyEs: On the last night of the festival dice cuándo ocurre la escena.

items.prompt: Which part of the festival sentence answers where?
items.text: On the last night of the festival, Leila waited nervously beside the stage while the crowd grew louder.
items.why: Beside the stage names a place, so it answers where.
items.whyEs: Beside the stage nombra un lugar, así que responde dónde.

items.prompt: Which question does the because part answer?
items.text: Leila's hands trembled because she had never sung in front of so many people.
items.why: Because she had never sung in front of so many people gives the reason, so it answers why.
items.whyEs: Because she had never sung in front of so many people da la razón, así que responde por qué.

items.prompt: Choose the detail that tells WHERE.
items.model: Leila waited beside the red curtain as the drums began.
items.why: Beside the red curtain is a place. Until sunrise tells when, and all by herself tells who is there.
items.whyEs: Beside the red curtain es un lugar. Until sunrise dice cuándo, y all by herself dice quién está.

items.prompt: Check every expansion of Leila waited that tells why.

options.text: Leila waited so that she could hear her friend perform first.
Leila waited beside the red curtain.
Leila waited because her turn was last.

items.why: So that she could hear... and because her turn was last give reasons. Beside the red curtain tells where, and after lunch tells when.
items.whyEs: So that she could hear... y because her turn was last dan razones. Beside the red curtain dice dónde, y after lunch dice cuándo.

items.prompt: Which is the strongest expansion of the kernel The crowd cheered?

options.text: Moments after the final note, the crowd in the courtyard cheered until the lanterns shook.

items.why: The last sentence adds when (moments after the final note) and where (in the courtyard), and it paints a vivid picture.
items.whyEs: La última oración agrega cuándo (moments after the final note) y dónde (in the courtyard), y crea una imagen vívida.

write.prompt: Expand the kernel sentence into a moment from a story. Tell when and where Leila walked onto the stage.
write.promptEs: Amplía la oración base en un momento de un cuento. Di cuándo y dónde Leila subió al escenario.
write.model: When the lights came on, Leila walked onto the stage in the town square and began to sing her favorite song.

familyTalk.en: Tell about a moment from your day in one short sentence. Then add when it happened, where you were, and why.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten un momento de su día en una oración corta. Luego agreguen cuándo ocurrió, dónde estaban y por qué.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to read the kernel and the expanded sentence aloud to hear how the details bring the scene to life.
teacherTip.es: Pide que lean en voz alta la oración base y la ampliada para escuchar cómo los detalles dan vida a la escena.
